card.text: Burnout: chronic workplace stress that hasn't been successfully managed (WHO)

events.text: The cleanest definition we have comes from the World Health Organization.

card.text: Burnout: chronic workplace stress that hasn't been successfully managed (WHO)

events.text: In twenty nineteen, in the eleventh edition of its International Classification of Diseases, it described burnout as a syndrome "resulting from chronic workplace stress that has not been successfully managed."

card.text: Burnout: chronic workplace stress that hasn't been successfully managed (WHO)

events.text: Chronic, and not successfully managed.
So it's not one bad week.
No.
It's stress that has gone on for a long time without anything changing.
And the W H O lists three dimensions.
First, feeling drained or exhausted.
Second, more mental distance from your job, or feeling negative and cynical about it.
Third, reduced professional efficacy, which is a formal way of saying you don't feel effective anymore.
Give me what those look like on a real shift.
Exhaustion is the person who looks like they've worked a full day when they clock in.

events.text: And reduced efficacy is your strongest person suddenly saying they're just not good at this job anymore.
That third one is sneaky, because it can look like a performance problem.
It often gets treated like one.
The Canadian Psychological Association has a fact sheet on workplace burnout.
The behaviours it lists include putting things off, pulling away from coworkers, more absences, and the opposite too, coming in to work while unwell.
The emotional signs include irritability, anxiety, and losing interest in work.
And there are physical ones, like ongoing fatigue, headaches and trouble sleeping.
Now, the W H O also said something specific about what burnout is not.
Two things.

events.text: So if someone says they're burned out on parenting, that's a real feeling, but it's not what this definition covers.

This definition is about the job.
Let's do stress versus burnout, because those get mixed up constantly.
The Canadian Psychological Association frames it simply.

events.text: Some researchers go further.

A twenty twenty four paper called Burnout, Fifty Years Later, argued that burnout can be hard to tell apart from depression, and warned that the burnout label could mean someone's depression goes untreated.
So what does that mean for a manager?
It means you don't decide which one it is.

events.text: In the early nineteen seventies, he volunteered as a counsellor at the Saint Mark's Free Clinic in the East Village.
He'd work full days at his private practice and then show up at the clinic in the evening.
And who did the clinic serve?
Mostly young people from the neighbourhood, and many of them used drugs.
According to one history of the term, burnout was actually slang among the clinic's patients for the effects of long term drug use.
Freudenberger himself pointed instead to the burned out buildings around the clinic as the image he had in mind.
So the word was already in the air.
